intent: Delete every ds:Signature element. SPs that treat a missing signature as 'no validation required' accept the unsigned assertion.
indicates: Relying party does not require a signature on the assertion/response.

intent: Wrap a forged, unsigned Assertion alongside a signed Response (or vice versa) where only the outer element is signed but the SP reads claims from the unsigned inner Assertion.
indicates: SP validates the Response signature but trusts assertion content that is outside the signed scope.

intent: Clone the signed Response, give the original a new ID, and place the forged Response (containing attacker NameID) as the parent. Signature still references the original ID.
indicates: SP resolves the signed reference but processes the first/forged Response element.

intent: Like XSW1 but the signature uses a detached (non-enveloped) reference; the forged Response sits as a sibling rather than a child.
indicates: Reference resolution and assertion processing target different elements.

intent: Insert a forged Assertion as a sibling BEFORE the original signed Assertion; both share document scope so the SP may pick the forged one first.
indicates: SP picks the first Assertion by position, validator validates the signed (later) one.

intent: Forged Assertion as a sibling AFTER the original, with the original moved inside the forged one as a child.
indicates: DOM order vs reference URI mismatch in assertion selection.

intent: Copy the original assertion and change attacker assertion's content while leaving the signature value pointing at the (now-relocated) original; exploits enveloped-signature transform handling.
indicates: Signature value validates a tree the SP does not actually consume.

intent: Place the original signed assertion (with its Signature) inside the Signature element of the forged assertion to confuse reference resolution.
indicates: Reference '' (whole-doc) or same-ID resolution selects original while content read is forged.

intent: Add an Extensions element with a forged assertion bearing the same ID as the original; ID uniqueness is not enforced so getElementById may return the wrong node.
indicates: getElementById returns first match; signed and processed nodes differ.

intent: For SPs using the legacy Object element: move the original assertion into a ds:Object inside the forged signature so it validates but is not the consumed assertion.
indicates: Signed ds:Object content ignored during assertion consumption.

intent: Inject an XML comment inside NameID (admin<!---->@victim) so canonicalization-vs-text-extraction differences make the SP read only 'admin'. Classic GitHub/Duo/OneLogin auth bypass class.
indicates: SP's text extraction differs from the canonicalizer that validated the signature.

intent: Replace the embedded ds:X509Certificate with an attacker certificate while keeping the original signature. SPs that trust the in-message cert (key-confusion / no trust pinning) re-validate against the attacker key.
indicates: SP validates the signature against the certificate embedded in the message rather than a pinned IdP certificate.
